name: Wikipedia collaborative encyclopedia
description: A network encyclopedia written and revised collaboratively by volunteer contributors and made available to readers without charge.

impact.note: Free volunteer-written reference in hundreds of languages, used across many countries; looking things up reorganised around it, with data and research projects built on it.

date.label: 15 January 2001
date.basis: Date or stated historical interval in cited source; see caveats.

events.statement: Wikipedia launched as a free encyclopedia that people could collaboratively edit.
events.caveats: Internet and suitable device access were required; later community rules and access restrictions varied.

evidence.supports: Foundation dates launch, describes free collaborative editing and language editions.

date.label: within first year
date.basis: Foundation retrospectively reports growth during the first year after launch.

events.statement: The Wikimedia Foundation reports that Wikipedia reached 18 language editions within its first year.
events.caveats: Language editions are not the number of writers, readers, countries, or equally complete translations.

evidence.supports: Foundation dates launch, describes free collaborative editing and language editions.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest sourced event establishing this scoped achievement; it is not a claim of global priority.

measures.subject: Wikipedia by the end of its first year
measures.conditions: Foundation retrospective; not a measure of readership or completeness.

evidence.supports: Foundation reports 18 languages within first year.

caveats: Other encyclopedias and collaborative wiki software predated Wikipedia. Editing policies, page protections, and availability vary over time.

research.note: New source-backed draft; independent review pending. Independent review: An online encyclopedia uses the Web, but that does not establish dependence on the specific 1991 FTP release; that exact-referent link was removed. Independent reader checked Wikimedia’s launch date and 18 languages within the first year; languages are not users.
